0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 11 November 1974, after the draft finalized by the Conveyors, Vertical Hoists and Bucket Elevators Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 The purchaser turer any statutory to when in use and conveyors shall be Guards shall also The manufacturer allowed for. shall, at the time of enquiry, disclose to the manufacrequirements to which the conveyor shall be subjected which are intended to ensure its safe working. The so constructed as to comply with these requirements. comply with the appropriate statutory requirements. shall inform the purchaser to the extent of guarding

0.3 A list of statutory provisions affecting conveyors in use in India is given in Appendix A. 0.4 While preparing this standard considerable assistance has been derived from BS 4531' : 1969 `Specification for portable and mobile troughed belt conveyors' , issued by the British Standards Institution. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

MATERIAL 3.1 The material used in the construction of the conveyors shall comply with, or be at least equivalent to the requirements specified in the appropriate Indian Standards. 4. *DIMENSIONS 4.1 Belt Widths The belt widths, b, shall be as follows:

300, 400, 500, 650, 800 and 1000 mm. 4.2 XcUer Arrangement - The idlers for portable and mobile conveyors consist of carrying and return idlers. The carrying idler set consists either of two idlers inclined to each other at a suitable angle to form a V or of a central idler and two side idlers. The idlers which support the return run of the belt consists of single idler. 4.3 Idler Diameters -The diameters, d,, of the idler shall be as follows: 101.6, 108, 115 and 127 mm.

4.4.2 Tilt - The tilt ( ~9), the angle formed by the projections of the side idler axis and the axis of the central idler on the belt plane in the case of S-idler sets [ see figure in Table 1 ), is a function of the idler inclination ( A ) and the belt speed. It should be as small as possible but shall not exceed 3". The tilt should be towards the direction of the belt run.

5. GENERAL

REQUIREMENTS

5.1 Belt Capacities md Speeds - Belt width and speed should, where possible, be chosen to make it operate under full load, special regard should be given to the nature, size-grading, characteristics and angle of repose of the material to be handled, and to the problems posed by high speed and the use of skirt plates. 5.2 Angle of Inclination - As portable and mobile conveyors can be made to move in a vertical plane, consideration should be given to the maximum angle of inclination depending on the material carried. 5.3 Take-Up Devices: A take-up device, to be approved shall be The recommended amount of take-up provided for all belt conveyors. for belt tensioning is given in Table 2. 5.4 Skirt Plates - Where skirt plates are fitted to feed chutes to guide the material into the centre of the belt and to prevent spillage, the average width between them shall, in general, be not more than two-thirds of the belt width. It is recommended that the total length of the feed hopper and its associated skirt plates should be not less than 1 200 mm, adjacent to the belt. 5.5 Luffing Gear - Luffing gear, where fitted, shall be self&taining, and shall not require a manual force of more than 147 N to operate. - Provision shall be made for the lubrication of bearings 5.6 Lubrication including ball and roller bearings. Where fitted, all lubricating points shall be readily accessible without removing the guards. 5.7 Power Unit - The power unit shall be and local conditions, and particular attention starting torque required. Electric motors, continuously and shall comply with IS: specified.

6. SAFETY

PRECAUTIONS

6.1 Access - Handrails and intermediate rails shall be fitted to all sloping gangways, and gangways from which a person is likely to fall a distance of more than 2 m, on the side remote from the conveyors, in addition to any handrail which may be required to guard the conveyor. The top rail shall be at least 1 m above the level of the walkway. A toeboard shall be placed at walkway level. 6.2 Guarding Guards shall be provided at: a) all pulleys and belt nips ( see Fig. 1 ) ; b)' carrying idlers and ( if accessible ) return idlers, where an upward movement of the belt may be restricted, for example, loading points and some convex curves, or where the tension in the belt is sufficient to give rise to risk of trapling; and c) Rotating shafts and couplings, chains and chain w-heels, gears, driving belts and pulleys, etc. Guards shall be securely fixed in position and shall be capable of removal and replacement without dismantling any other part. 7

FIG. 1

LAYOVT OF A MOBILE BELT CONVEYOR SHOWING NIP I'orr;rs

IS I 7465 - 1974
6.3 Size of Mesh Opening and Clearance - The minimum clearance between the guard and the moving parts and the size of opening in guards of perforated metal, woven wire or similar material shall be in accordance with the following reqgrements: Size

of

Opening

Minimum

Clearance

mm Not exceeding 10 Over 10, up to and including 13 Over 13, up to and including 30 Over 30, up to and including 38

mm 25 65 100 130

The size of opening shall be taken to refer to the maximum dimension df the opening, except that where the openings are in the form of slots, the length may be ignored if the width does not exceed 13 mm. 6.3.1 Slots 30 mm wide, suitably reinforced, may be provided in guards for the insertion of bars for cleaning. The minimum distance between any moving part of the conveyor and any part of the slot shall be 300 mm. 6.3.2 Guards for nip points between belts and pulleys shall either prevent access to the nip or extend at least 1 m from the nip. 6.4 Safe Starting and Emergency StoppingAll starting operations on the conveyor should be preceded by an inspection to ensure that it is Means shall be provided at suitable points for stopping the safe to start. conveyor in an emergency. Starting after an emergency or accidental stoppage should not only be preceded by the inspection referred to above, but should also be allowed only after the inspection has determined the cause of the emergency or accidental stoppage, and the fault has been rectified.
7. MARKING

7.1 The portable and mobile troughed belt conveyors shall be marked with the following information on the name plate provided on the conveyor at suitable prominent place: a) Manufacturer's 7.1.1 Mark. identification, and with the IS1 Certification b) Any other information required by the purchaser.

The conveyor may also be marked

Nope - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard

9

IS t 7465 - 1974
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined @cm of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1

Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
